explanations: The nonce is a prefix derived only from the key id plus an in-memory counter that starts at 0 in every FieldCipher. Every replica, and every process after a restart, therefore produces the same nonce sequence under the same key. AES-GCM is a stream cipher underneath, so two messages under the same key and nonce share a keystream (c1 XOR c2 = p1 XOR p2), and nonce reuse also lets an attacker forge auth tags. A counter nonce is only safe when the counter is unique across every encryptor using the key, which nothing here guarantees. Drawing a fresh 12-byte nonce from randomBytes for each message removes the shared state; the envelope already stores the nonce, so old blobs still decrypt.
